intro: For JavaScript and TypeScript developers who want to test their code with Vitest 5, the Vite-powered test runner with a Jest-compatible API. You'll write and run tests, mock dependencies, measure coverage, test components in a real browser and organise larger test suites.
assumedKnowledge: JavaScript or TypeScript with ES modules and async/await
Helpful: a Vite-based project (Vitest works without one too)

steps.title: Install Vitest and write your first test
steps.goal: Add Vitest to a project, write a test with test and expect, and run it in watch mode.
steps.explanation: Install vitest as a dev dependency, add a "test": "vitest" script, and put tests in files ending in .test.js or .spec.js. Vitest reruns affected tests as you save.
steps.versionNote: Vitest 5 requires Node.js 22.12+ and Vite 6.4+; Vite is now a peer dependency.

steps.title: Learn the core features and assertions
steps.goal: Structure tests with describe, test and hooks, and check results with expect matchers.
steps.explanation: Vitest shares Vite's config and transforms, so TypeScript and JSX work without extra setup. Group tests with describe, use beforeEach/afterEach for setup, and use the expect API for assertions, including async ones.
steps.versionNote: In Vitest 5, unawaited expect(...).resolves and .rejects make the test fail, and toThrow('') matches any error message.

steps.title: Run the tests you want from the CLI
steps.goal: Run all tests, a single file or tests matching a name, and use CI-friendly run mode.
steps.explanation: vitest starts watch mode in development and vitest run runs once (as in CI). Filter by file path or by test name with -t, and use .only and .skip while working.
steps.versionNote: Vitest 5 joins suite and test names with ' > ' when matching -t / testNamePattern, so name filters written for older versions may need updating.

steps.title: Mock functions, modules and timers
steps.goal: Replace dependencies with mocks and spies, mock whole modules, and control time with fake timers.
steps.explanation: vi.fn() and vi.spyOn() record calls and return values; vi.mock() replaces a module; vi.useFakeTimers() lets you advance time instantly. Mock what is slow or unpredictable, such as network calls and dates.
steps.versionNote: Vitest 5 clears mock call history before each test by default (clearMocks: true). vi.mock, vi.unmock and vi.hoisted must be at the top level of the file; calling them inside functions or blocks now throws. Fake timers also mock Temporal.

steps.title: Use snapshots wisely
steps.goal: Capture output with snapshot and inline snapshot tests, and review changes deliberately.
steps.explanation: Snapshots store a serialized value and fail when it changes. They're useful for large, stable outputs; review snapshot updates like code rather than accepting them blindly.

steps.title: Choose a test environment and use test context
steps.goal: Run tests in Node or a simulated DOM, and use fixtures from the test context for shared setup.
steps.explanation: The environment option picks node, jsdom or happy-dom per project or file. The test context gives each test helpers and lets you define reusable fixtures with test.extend.

steps.title: Measure coverage
steps.goal: Generate coverage reports and set thresholds that fail the build when coverage drops.
steps.explanation: Enable coverage with the v8 or istanbul provider to see which lines your tests run, and set thresholds in config so coverage can't silently fall.
steps.versionNote: In Vitest 5, coverage include/exclude patterns match paths relative to the project root, and glob thresholds no longer inherit perFile.

steps.title: Test components in a real browser
steps.goal: Run component tests in real browsers with Browser Mode instead of a simulated DOM.
steps.explanation: Browser Mode runs tests in an actual browser through a provider such as Playwright, so layout, events and browser APIs behave like production. Locators find elements the way users do.
steps.versionNote: In Vitest 5, browser locators match exactly by default, and render is async in vitest-browser-vue and vitest-browser-svelte.

steps.title: Organise larger suites with projects and reporters
steps.goal: Run different configurations (for example unit and browser tests) as projects, and choose reporters for CI.
steps.explanation: Projects let one Vitest run cover several configurations or packages. Reporters control output: readable in the terminal, JSON or JUnit files for CI, or the HTML report.
steps.versionNote: In Vitest 5, inline projects inherit the root config by default, json and junit reporters write to files rather than stdout, and output goes under .vitest/.

steps.title: Debug, speed up and migrate from Jest
steps.goal: Debug failing tests, fix common errors, make large suites faster, and move an existing Jest suite to Vitest.
steps.explanation: Debug tests in your editor or browser devtools, check the common-errors guide when setup fails, and tune pools and isolation for speed. Vitest's API is close to Jest's, and the Jest migration guide lists the differences.
